title: Oil & Filter Service
subtitle: Fresh oil keeps your engine quiet, clean, and long-lived — I'll walk you through it step by step.
tone: Coach Mode: warm mentor, short sentences, celebrate progress, never shame. Prefer visuals over walls of text. Always offer DIY vs shop without judgment.
prerequisites: Engine cool enough to touch the drain area safely (warm is OK; hot is not)
Correct oil viscosity for this vehicle (check door-jamb sticker or owner's manual)
New oil filter that fits your year/make/model/engine
Drain pan rated for at least your oil capacity + 1 qt spare
tools_checklist: Jack + jack stands or ramps (if needed for access)
parts_checklist: Drain plug washer / crush washer (replace if required)
Optional: engine oil drain plug if threads are damaged

adaptive_rules.coach_note: For most gas engines on full synthetic, plan oil + filter around every 5,000–7,500 miles (or per your manual — manuals win).
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Use the viscosity printed on the door jamb (often 0W-20 or 5W-30 in the US).

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Hybrids still need oil changes — short trips and Atkinson-cycle engines benefit from staying on schedule even if the ICE runs less often.
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Many hybrids specify 0W-16 or 0W-20 — confirm on the oil-cap / door sticker before buying.

adaptive_rules.coach_note: You're past 100k — great job maintaining it. Stick closer to the shorter end of the interval and inspect for leaks while you're under there.
Newer vehicle — follow the first oil-change window in the manual (often earlier than the long synthetic interval).
Diesel oil specs are stricter (CJ-4 / CK-4 class, etc.). Don't substitute regular gas-engine oil.
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Match diesel API / ACEA rating exactly — wrong oil can hurt emissions systems.

adaptive_rules.coach_note: This brand often wants specific OEM-approved oil (LL-01, MB 229.x, etc.). If you're unsure of the approval code, a dealer or indie specialist oil change is a smart call.
Battery EVs don't have engine oil services. If you meant cabin or gearbox fluid, tell me and we'll switch scenarios.

steps.title: Let's protect that engine
steps.description: You're doing the right thing by staying on oil service. I'll confirm your vehicle and mileage, then we'll choose DIY or a shop — either path is a win.
steps.visual_prompt: Hero still of oil + filter kit

action_buttons.label: Update vehicle / mileage
action_buttons.payload: Please update my year, make, model, engine, and current mileage before oil service.

variants.title: Quick check — this may not apply
variants.description: Battery EVs don't take engine oil. If you meant another fluid, tell me in chat and I'll route you.

steps.title: Are you due?
steps.description: We'll match your mileage and powertrain to a sensible interval. Your owner's manual always overrides generic advice.

action_buttons.label: Not sure — coach me
action_buttons.payload: Help me decide if my oil change is due based on my mileage and last service date.

variants.description: High-mile champion — lean toward ~5,000-mile synthetic intervals and peek for leaks while you're under the car.
Hybrid note: even if the gas engine naps a lot, keep oil fresh — moisture and fuel dilution still happen on short trips.
Early ownership window — check the break-in / first service page in the manual before stretching to long synthetic intervals.

steps.title: DIY or let a shop handle it?
steps.description: DIY usually lands around $45–$120 in parts and ~45 minutes if you have safe access. A shop is often $80–$180 and faster — perfect if you're short on tools, space, or OEM oil approvals.
steps.safety_warning: If you cannot use jack stands or ramps safely, choose a shop. Never work under a car supported only by a jack.

variants.description: Luxury tip: confirm the OEM oil approval code first. If the bottle doesn't list it, a specialist quick-lube or dealer oil service avoids expensive mistakes.
variants.safety_warning: Wrong oil approval on some European engines can affect warranty conversations — when unsure, shop it.

steps.title: Parts check (visual)
steps.description: Grab oil (correct viscosity + quantity), a matching filter, and a new crush washer if your plug needs one. Snap a photo of your oil cap / door sticker if you want me to double-check the spec.

variants.description: Confirm capacity for your hybrid engine — some take less volume than the non-hybrid twin. Cap sticker + manual beat memory.
Diesel: verify API/ACEA rating on the jug, not just viscosity.

steps.title: Safety setup before you crawl under
steps.description: Park level, engage park/brake, chock wheels. Lift only if needed — stands on pinch welds, then give the car a firm shake test. Gloves on.
steps.safety_warning: Never rely on a jack alone. If the car feels unstable, stop and use a shop. Hot exhaust and catalytic converters burn skin — stay clear.

steps.title: Drain the old oil
steps.description: Place the pan under the drain plug. Crack the plug loose with a wrench, finish by hand, and let it drain fully. Keep the plug and washer somewhere clean.
steps.safety_warning: Oil can be hot enough to burn. Loosen slowly — the last threads release a sudden flow. Don't let the plug drop into a full pan of hot oil.

action_buttons.label: Plug won't budge / stripped
action_buttons.payload: My oil drain plug is stuck or feels like it might strip. What should I do next?

steps.title: Swap the oil filter
steps.description: Remove the old filter (expect a little spill). Wipe the mount clean. Film the new rubber gasket with fresh oil, then install hand-tight — usually 3/4 to 1 turn after contact (follow the filter box).
steps.safety_warning: Cross-threading a filter can dump oil onto a hot exhaust. Start by hand only. Cartridge-style filters: replace O-rings and seat the housing to the torque in the manual.

action_buttons.label: Old filter won't come off
action_buttons.payload: My oil filter is stuck. Coach me through safe removal options.

variants.description: Many of these use a top-side cartridge filter — replace all O-rings, oil them lightly, and torque the cap to spec (guessing hand-tight is how housings crack).

steps.title: Refill & verify level
steps.description: Reinstall the drain plug with a new washer if needed (torque to spec when you can). Refill with a funnel to just under capacity, start the engine 30–60 seconds, shut off, wait a minute, then read the dipstick. Top off to the safe range — don't overfill.
steps.safety_warning: Check under the car for fresh drips before you lower it fully. Overfilling can damage seals and catalytic converters — add gradually.

action_buttons.label: Level is high / low
action_buttons.payload: My oil level is not in the correct dipstick range after a refill. Help me correct it safely.

action_buttons.label: I see a leak
action_buttons.payload: I see oil leaking after my oil change. Where should I look first and is it safe to drive?

steps.title: Reset reminder & log the win
steps.description: Reset the oil maintenance light if your model has one, then save this service to your vehicle health file with mileage and oil type. I'll remind you before the next interval.

action_buttons.label: How do I reset the oil light?
action_buttons.payload: How do I reset the oil maintenance reminder on my vehicle?

completion.title: Oil service complete — nice work
completion.description: You just bought your engine quieter miles. Default next check: about 5,000–7,500 miles (we'll adapt to your powertrain and manual). Keep a photo of the receipt / oil jug in your health file.

action_buttons.label: Ask a follow-up
action_buttons.payload: I just finished an oil and filter change. Any post-service checks I should do this week?
